question: Why can electromagnetic waves travel through vacuum, while mechanical waves cannot? Give reason in terms of field variation.

options.A: Electromagnetic waves consist of time-varying electric and magnetic fields. A changing electric field produces a magnetic field and a changing magnetic field produces an electric field, so they sustain propagation even in vacuum. Mechanical waves need material particles to transmit a disturbance.
options.B: Electromagnetic waves travel in vacuum because vacuum contains charged particles, whereas mechanical waves cannot travel because they have no energy.
options.C: Electromagnetic waves travel through vacuum because their electric field is constant; mechanical waves require changing magnetic fields.
options.D: Mechanical waves need no medium, whereas electromagnetic waves need air so that the electric and magnetic fields can travel.
